faqs.title: Frequently asked questions
faqs.intro: Common questions about OpenPanel's MCP server.

items.question: Which AI clients work with OpenPanel MCP?
items.answer: Any client that speaks MCP over streamable HTTP. The settings page writes the config for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code (Copilot) and Raycast, and the same URL and token work in an agent you build yourself.

items.question: Do I need to install anything?
items.answer: No. The MCP server is hosted by OpenPanel at `https://api.openpanel.dev/mcp`. You add that URL to your AI client's config with your token—nothing runs on your machine.

items.question: How does authentication work?
items.answer: Your token is `base64(clientId:clientSecret)`. Generate it with `echo -n "CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET" | base64` and send it as an `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN` header. If your client can't set headers, append it to the URL as `?token=YOUR_TOKEN` instead—it works the same, but a token in a URL is easier to leak into history and logs.

items.question: What's the difference between a read client and a root client?
items.answer: A read client is tied to one project and gets the 39 read tools. A root client can reach every project in the organization and adds the 9 tools that create and edit dashboards and reports. Write clients cannot authenticate with MCP at all.

items.question: Can the AI modify my data?
items.answer: With a read client, no: its 39 tools only read. A root client also gets 9 write tools that create, update, delete and lay out dashboards and reports, so treat a root token as write access. Neither can change events, profiles or settings.

items.question: Does it work with self-hosted OpenPanel?
items.answer: If you're self-hosting, the MCP server is part of the API—it runs on your instance at the same `/mcp` path. Point your AI client at your own API URL instead of `api.openpanel.dev`.

items.question: How is this different from the Google Analytics MCP server?
items.answer: Google Analytics MCP connects to GA4 data—pageviews, traffic sources, sessions. OpenPanel's MCP connects to product event data: custom events, user profiles, funnels, retention cohorts. If you want to ask 'what's the 30-day retention for users who completed onboarding', that's not a question GA4's MCP can answer. OpenPanel's can.
